summary: The note surveys how financial aid and scholarships are adapting to the growing number of adults returning to education. It describes the financial barriers adult learners face and the responses emerging from governments, universities, corporations, grant-makers and crowdfunding platforms. Examples include Metro State University's Second Chance Scholarship, ByteWise's Aspire Scholarship, and the stories of learners such as Michael Thompson and Helen Ramirez.
one_line: Overview of emerging financial aid, scholarships, grants and crowdfunding options helping adult learners return to education, with examples from 2023-2024.
key_facts: Michael Thompson, a 45-year-old former manufacturing supervisor, returned to education as his industry evolved; in an October 3, 2023 interview he said he needed to upgrade his skills to stay relevant.
Dr. Linda Ferguson of the Urban Education Institute published findings on September 20, 2023 saying the main deterrent for adult learners is 'not a lack of will, but a lack of means.'
Adult learners face financial barriers such as mortgages, childcare and existing debt alongside tuition fees.
Canada's 'Lifelong Learning Plan' has served as a prototype for policies worldwide.
In the United States, legislation introduced after September 2023 aims to expand Pell Grant eligibility and award amounts for adults who are part-time students or previously entered the workforce.
Metro State University launched the 'Second Chance Scholarship' on November 5, 2023 for adults out of school more than five years; it covers up to 50% of tuition for eligible candidates.
Tech company ByteWise announced the 'Aspire Scholarship' on December 1, 2023, targeting adult learners seeking to improve digital literacy.
The 'Future Innovators Scholarship' opened for applications on January 15, 2024 and targets adults interested in fast-changing technological sectors.
Helen Ramirez, a 38-year-old single mother of two, received the 'New Horizons Grant' in February 2024 and is studying nursing.
Grants do not require repayment, and are offered to adults with financial need or those studying high-demand fields like healthcare or education.
Joshua Bell, a budding entrepreneur, used Indiegogo on March 4, 2024 to crowdfund a specialized business analytics program.
Crowdfunding platforms such as GoFundMe and Kickstarter have seen successful campaigns for educational goals.
